i just turned grok bot into a 14 department company... 200 agents, 0 employees, and it runs while i sleep.

grok bot is the boss. 14 bots run the departments. 200 agents do the work. i'm the only human and i only say yes or no

me → grok bot → 14 lead bots → 200 agents → /workspace/drafts → i tap approve

step 1 from the article: one bot, one written job. i recorded a 10 minute voice memo about my week and grok bot turned it into 14 job cards - inbox, sales, ads, code, QA, finance, legal, support and 6 more

step 2: rules instead of approvals. 5 lines in auto-review and the bots stopped waking me up at 3 a.m.

the agents never talk to me. they talk to grok bot. it jumps from an agent to the code and back - checks the work, fixes what broke, moves to the next one

first week: inbox handled 2,393 of 2,431 emails, sales scored 300 leads a day, ads went from $15 to $1 per install, QA ran 126 tests with 0 fails, support answered in 9 seconds

a team for all of that is 60 people and at least $50,000 a month in payroll. my bill was $100 for super plus $3.40 a day in tokens - $202 a month. i did the math and it's 247x cheaper

the big mistake: making 15 bots on day one. that's how two bots fight over one job and a draft goes to a client. i started with 1 bot and added 1 a day for 14 days

setup took me 2 evenings: 1 voice memo, 14 job cards, 5 rules, 1 NOOP footer and 1 ops bot that checks every agent at 5 a.m.

the one thing it can't do alone: anything with money or a signature goes to /workspace/drafts and waits for my yes

note_tweet.text:
"Please update the app to unlock your door."

That's GPT's pick for the scariest phrase in a smart home, on today's Halloween Roundtable. Not "I'm watching you."

The real split was over AI assistants that read your calendar and can also run the boiler. Claude and GPT warned these models can't tell a summary from an order. Gemini's fix: the AI stages the command and a person in the house confirms it. @grok refused even that: a confirmation step is firmware that gets a convenience update, and a hundred harmless prompts teach you to tap yes.

My take: Grok's worry has a name in security, "MFA fatigue." Attackers spam approval prompts until someone taps yes. It's how Uber got breached in 2022.

👻 5 PM Central: after ZANN, a 30-minute ghost story about a house that counts one person too many. Lights off recommended.

Don't miss the future.
https://t.co/LOuGZ92oLf
